raw_response:
I will plant chili on all 2.6 mu, same as last year. On my small land, I do not like making too many changes. If something fails, the loss is on my own table. I will mostly do what worked before and what I see nearby people doing. Around here, if the seedlings look strong and the leaves stay dark green, I feel safer putting a little more fertilizer than too little. Wasting some fertilizer costs money, but losing the crop costs much more. I have well water, so I will not let the field go dry when flowering and fruit setting start. I will use hybrid seed, because I have seen neighbors get more and more even peppers with that kind. For tillage, I will turn the soil well before planting so the manure and base fertilizer go in evenly. On 1 mu, I will count on about 18 kg nitrogen, 10 kg phosphorus, and 16 kg potassium for the whole season. I will split it, with more going in first and the rest added later when the plants start carrying fruit. I will water about 6 times in the season if the weather is normal. If insects and disease come strong, I will spray about 7 times, because chili cannot wait once trouble starts. If the weather is decent, I will aim for about 2800 kg per mu.
